title: Do they hold the keys to your Lord's treasures?
subtitle: Who is actually in charge
then: The Quraysh chiefs acted as if they decided who deserved a prophet. Allah asks: {trap}do they hold the keys to His treasures?{/trap} The tafsir answers, {reward}never; Allah is the only King and Owner of existence{/reward}, and He does what He wills.
now: You watch someone else get the job, the baby, the blessing, and you quietly feel it should have been decided differently. {idea}The treasures are His, not yours or theirs.{/idea}
old: I know better who deserves what.
new: Allah holds the treasures, and He gives as He wills, wisely.
try: Next time you feel envy, say MashaAllah for the other person and ask Allah for good for yourself.

title: Do they have a ladder to heaven to hear its news?
subtitle: Show the proof
then: Do they have {trap}a stairway to heaven{/trap}, where the angels are, to hear things? Then {idea}let their listener produce manifest proof.{/idea} The tafsir says {trap}they will never be able to do so.{/trap}
now: Someone in the family chat is sure about what will happen, what Allah wants, who is going to Hell. They speak like they heard it directly. {idea}Ask: what is your proof?{/idea} Ask yourself the same.
old: If I feel sure about something in religion, I must be right.
new: Claims about the unseen need proof from Allah, not just confidence.
try: Before repeating a religious claim today, check its source first.

title: They gave Allah daughters while wanting sons for themselves.
subtitle: A double standard exposed

row.title: sons for ourselves
sub: faces dark at a girl's birth

then: The pagans preferred sons, and when told of a daughter, {trap}a man's face would turn dark with suppressed anger{/trap}, says the tafsir. Yet {trap}they made the angels Allah's daughters{/trap} and worshipped them. The verse exposes the contradiction.
now: You hold others to rules you never apply to yourself. The colleague is lazy, but you are tired. Your cousin is stingy, but you are careful. {idea}A double standard tells on the heart.{/idea}
new: When I judge others by one rule and myself by another, something is wrong in me.
try: Catch one double standard in yourself today and apply your rule to yourself instead.

title: He asks no payment. Why act as if he sends a bill?
subtitle: Free guidance, treated like a debt
then: The surah introduction says they {trap}avoided him as if he was asking them for a reward.{/trap} Allah asks: do you ask them a wage, {trap}so they are weighed down with debt?{/trap} The tafsir says no, he asked for nothing.
now: A friend gives you honest advice for free, and you react like they handed you an invoice. {reward}Good counsel that costs you nothing is a gift.{/reward}
old: Advice from others is a burden on me.
new: Honest guidance given freely is a gift, not a debt.
try: Thank the last person who gave you honest advice, even if it stung.

title: Do they know the unseen, writing it down?
subtitle: Only Allah knows what is hidden
then: Do they have the unseen, {trap}so they write it down?{/trap} The tafsir says they do not, for {idea}none in the heavens or earth knows the unseen except Allah.{/idea} Their confidence about the Hereafter had no basis.
now: You are sure you will have time to repent later, sure your plans for ten years will work out, sure you know how someone's story ends. {idea}None of that is written in your hand.{/idea}
old: I know how things will turn out.
new: The future is with Allah, so I act well today.
try: Replace one I will later with something you do today.

title: Their plot turns back on the plotters.
subtitle: Schemes against the truth
then: The surah introduction says the chiefs {trap}took counsel together to devise schemes{/trap} against the Prophet ﷺ. Allah says the disbelievers are the ones plotted against. The tafsir explains: {idea}their plots will only harm them.{/idea}
now: You plan how to get back at the coworker who embarrassed you: the cc on the email, the comment in the meeting. {idea}Schemes have a way of coming home.{/idea} Let it go, and let Allah handle it.
old: If I plan carefully, I can get back at them.
new: Scheming harms the schemer most. I can leave the account with Allah.
try: Drop one small plan to get even with someone today.

title: Is there any god but Allah? Glory to Him above it.
subtitle: The last question in the chain
then: After a long string of or do they questions, the last one: {trap}or have they a god other than Allah?{/trap} The tafsir calls it {idea}a harsh refutation{/idea} of calling on rivals with Him, then Allah {reward}glorifies Himself above their idolatry.{/reward}
now: You may not have idols, but you have things you cannot say no to: approval, the scale, the salary figure. {idea}Ask which of them you obey like a god.{/idea} Then say SubhanAllah and mean it.
old: Idolatry is something from the past.
new: Anything I obey over Allah is a rival. He is above them all.
try: Say SubhanAllah 33 times after one prayer today, thinking of what it means.

title: Even a falling sky, they would call just clouds.
subtitle: When no sign is ever enough
then: The tafsir says that if punishment came at them from the sky, {trap}they would not believe it was coming their way{/trap}. They would call it layers of clouds. It cites another verse: given a gate to heaven, {trap}they would say our eyes are dazzled.{/trap}
now: The third warning from your doctor. The friend who drifts away after the same argument. You call it bad timing each time. {idea}At some point, the clouds are not clouds.{/idea}
old: Each warning I get is just a coincidence.
new: A heart that explains away every sign will never see one.
try: Take one repeated warning in your life seriously today, and write down what it might be telling you.

title: Leave them until they meet their Day.
subtitle: Not every argument is yours to win
then: After the clouds verse, Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}leave them alone{/idea} until they meet their Day. The tafsir says this is {trap}the Day of Resurrection{/trap}, when they will faint in terror.
now: You have argued with the same person about faith for years. Every holiday dinner, round two. {idea}You can stop.{/idea} Live well, make dua, and leave the final word to Allah.
old: If I stop arguing, I am giving up on them.
new: Sometimes stepping back and leaving it to Allah is the right step.
try: Skip one argument you know will go nowhere, and make dua for that person instead.

title: That Day, all their scheming will be worth nothing.
subtitle: Plans that will not help
then: The chiefs had held council after council. The tafsir says {trap}their deceit and plots{/trap} shall not help them in the least on that Day, {trap}nor will they be helped.{/trap}
now: You are good at angles: the clever excuse, the right contact, the loophole. It works at work and with the tax forms. {idea}None of it works on that Day.{/idea} {reward}Only honest deeds do.{/reward}
old: With the right strategy, I can get out of anything.
new: On the Day, no strategy helps. Only what I did sincerely.
try: Choose the straight way today in one place where you usually take a clever shortcut.

title: Smaller trials come first, so people might return.
subtitle: Hardship as a wake-up call
then: The tafsir says Allah tests them with {trap}various hardships in this world{/trap} so {reward}they might go back and repent{/reward}, citing a verse about the near torment. But most {trap}revert to the worst of what they did{/trap} once it is lifted.
now: The scare, the layoff, the night in the ER. You promised Allah you would change. Then it passed and so did the promise. {idea}The hard days were the invitation.{/idea}
old: Hard times are just bad luck to get through.
new: Hardships can be Allah calling me back before it is too late.
try: Remember one promise you made to Allah in a hard time. Keep a piece of it today.

title: Be patient. You are under Our eyes.
subtitle: Seen and protected
then: After all their insults, Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}be patient{/idea}, for {reward}you are under Our eyes and protection.{/reward} Then: glorify Him when you rise. The tafsir mentions rising for prayer, from sleep, and the hadith of saying SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik before leaving a gathering.
now: The meeting where you were talked over. The scroll of comments under your post. You feel unseen and alone. {reward}You are seen.{/reward} Patience is lighter when you know Who is watching.
old: No one sees what I put up with.
new: Allah sees me and protects me, so I can be patient.
try: Before leaving your next gathering, say SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik.

title: Praise Him at night, and as the stars fade.
subtitle: The surah ends at dawn

key.label: What those two rak'ahs are worth

then: The tafsir says the night glorification means {idea}reciting the Quran and praying at night.{/idea} The setting of the stars refers to the two sunnah rak'ahs before Fajr. Aishah said the Prophet ﷺ was never more regular in any voluntary prayer, and he said {reward}they are better than this world and all in it.{/reward}
now: The alarm goes off before Fajr and the bed is warm. Two extra rak'ahs take three minutes. {reward}Better than everything in your bank account, your feed, your plans.{/reward} The stars are fading anyway.
old: The extra prayers before Fajr are too small to matter.
new: Two quiet rak'ahs as the stars fade are worth more than the whole world.
try: Tomorrow, pray the two rak'ahs before Fajr, even if quickly.
